text:
Maine's aphorism is often misread as a prediction or law of inevitable historical progress toward contract. He offered it as a description of how the law of *progressive* societies had moved so far ("hitherto"), and he did not say that movement must continue. His notion of "status" is also misrepresented: it meant legal capacities fixed by family position, such as patria potestas, and not social standing or all non-contractual relations in general.

CONFIDENCE: 80
